There's also some purplish coloration visible on background plants. Key features: broad bleached stripes parallel to leaf veins, no lesions or pustules.

Top candidates: **Stewarts_wilt** (bleached leaf streaks along leaf length), **Maize_streak_virus**, **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**, **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma**.

The Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus reference (top-right panel) is a very strong visual match — same red soil, same broad pale/cream longitudinal stripes, same reddish-purple background plants. Let me confirm by checking the remaining candidates.
None of those classes match. The test image's broad pale/cream longitudinal stripes clearly distinguish it. Let me view a few more reference images to be thorough before finalizing.

None of those match. My analysis is clear:

**Test image features:**
- Broad, creamy-white to pale-yellow longitudinal stripes running the full length of the leaf blade
- No discrete lesions, pustules, or spots — purely striped/streaked pattern
- Small scattered pale flecks visible on the leaf surface
- Red soil background; reddish-purple plants visible in background

**Comparison to candidates:**
- **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**: Reference top-right panel is an extremely close match — same broad pale/cream longitudinal stripes, same red soil, same reddish-purple background plants. MDMV description: "yellowing mosaic or mottle pattern," "narrow, light green to yellow vein streaks"
- **Maize_streak_virus**: Reference shows finer, more numerous narrow alternating streaks — different from the broad stripes in the test image
- **Stewarts_wilt**: Reference shows only early seedling stage; bleached streaks but different texture
- **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma**: Shows reddish-purple coloration at maturity — different pattern
- All other candidates (Gray leaf spot, NCLB, Eyespot, Physoderma, Goss wilt) show discrete lesions — ruled out

The broad creamy-white longitudinal striping is the hallmark of **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus** based on the strong visual match to the reference collage.
